label: Fused prefill sconv
mechanism: the four window-4 sconv sites of every prefill layer run as one Triton kernel instead of an fp32 conv1d chain, deleting ~36 bytes/element of HBM traffic for a 4-tap dot and the channel-major layout the chain leaked into the residual stream
hypothesis: model.sconv_prefill is the last bring-up-era eager chain left in the prefill layer and it runs FOUR times per layer (attention K, attention V, attention output, MoE output — modeling_inkling.py:500-542), i.e. 264 times per traversal. Every call does the whole window-4 depthwise convolution in fp32 through torch: xf = x.float() (read bf16, write fp32); conv1d(xf.transpose(1,2), ...) whose transposed input is not contiguous, so ATen copies it before the depthwise conv reads and writes another fp32 [B,C,T]; conv.transpose(1,2) + xf (two fp32 reads, one fp32 write); .to(bf16). That is ~36 bytes of HBM traffic per element to compute a dot with four terms. Per layer the four sites carry 6144 + 6144 + 2048 + 2048 = 16,384 channels per token (1024-wide K/V on the 11 global layers), so a canonical cohort moves GBs per layer on devices exp-0023's DEADENDS finding 1 shows are SATURATED during prefill (utilization.gpu 92-100% on the active device of the layer split, sampled every 0.4 s DURING the worker's own canonical bench). ONE VARIABLE: kernels/sconv_prefill.py (new) plus the fused branch in model.sconv_prefill behind PYENGINE_FUSED_SCONV=0, which reads the module global at call time; the eager chain is retained verbatim behind it and still serves non-CUDA / non-depthwise callers. One @triton.jit body: a program owns a [64, 256] tile of one batch row, loads the four shifted input tiles (out-of-range history reads 0.0 — causal_conv1d_fn's left pad), accumulates in fp32 in ASCENDING TAP ORDER so weight[..., -1] taps the current token (:461-481, cross-correlation, no kernel flip), adds the module's own-input residual in fp32 (:515+:542) and stores one bf16 round. The decode path is untouched (exp-0008's pooled sconv), so nothing inside the captured graph moves. UNLIKE every other fused kernel in this engine, the arithmetic does not change: a 4-term dot has one sensible order and it is the reference's. EVIDENCE, ISOLATED (engine/pyengine/tests/t_fused_sconv, GPU 4, B=6 T=1408, log /workspace/logs/t_fused_sconv_exp0025_out.log): (arm a) EQUIVALENCE is BITWISE at all six real site shapes x both dtypes — 0 mismatches of 17,301,504 (C=2048), 51,904,512 (C=6144) and 8,650,752 (C=1024) elements, max|delta| exactly 0.000e+00 — and also bitwise when the INPUT is itself channel-major, which the engine feeds forward. (arm b) two identical calls bitwise equal (the t_b3-adapted determinism arm; fixed grid, no atomics, no autotune). (arm c) SPEED, CUDA-event timed, interleaved arms after discarded warm-ups: attn K/V (SWA, C=2048) 0.376 -> 0.026 ms (14.5x), attn out and MoE out (C=6144) 1.088 -> 0.063 ms (17.2x), global K/V (C=1024) 0.195 -> 0.025 ms (7.9x); a SWA layer's four sites go 2.927 -> 0.178 ms = 16.4x, -2.749 ms/layer, i.e. -0.181 s per 66-layer traversal at that shape, repeats agreeing to 0.001 ms. (arm d) LAYOUT, the second half of the same mechanism: `conv.transpose(1,2) + xf` inherits the TRANSPOSED operand's strides, so the eager result is channel-major ([B,T,C] with strides (T*C, 1, T)) and every downstream consumer inherits it — the per-head K rmsnorm reduces over a stride-T axis, the exp-0023 attention kernel reads K/V with a stride-T head_dim, and `x = x + h` in layer_prefill propagates it into the residual stream so the NEXT layer's input_layernorm reduces a strided hidden axis too. The kernel stores where its consumers read: on the same values, the per-head rmsnorm goes 0.762 -> 0.594 ms and the residual add 0.218 -> 0.049 ms (4.4x). EVIDENCE, IN SITU on the real resident model through the real Scheduler, the arm exp-0011's rejection and exp-0018's null say must decide it (engine/pyengine/tests/t_fused_sconv_insitu, GPUs 4-7, ONE resident load, layer split [16,17,16,17], 8 already-decoding residents plus a 6-row cohort at ISL 690-800, arms INTERLEAVED off/on/off/on after discarded warm-ups of BOTH arms; log /workspace/logs/t_fused_sconv_insitu_exp0025_out.log): the PREFILL-only step (8 rows) goes 0.966 -> 0.804 s = 1.202x (-163 ms) and the MIXED step (6 prefill + 8 decode) 0.771 -> 0.646 s = 1.194x (-125 ms), with repeats agreeing to 0.008 s (0.973/0.960 vs 0.808/0.800; 0.775/0.768 vs 0.647/0.646); DECODE-ONLY steps do not move (0.073/0.074/0.067 s in both arms), as they must not — decode has used the pooled sconv since exp-0008. Schedule total 1.952 -> 1.663 s = 1.174x. NUMERICS, stated plainly because the in-situ tokens DO move (9 of 14 sequences over a 56-token schedule): the kernel is bitwise (arm a), so the drift cannot be its arithmetic, and arm f isolates the actual source on identical values in the two layouts — a GEMM is BITWISE across the layout change (max|d| 0.000e+00), but torch's rmsnorm is NOT, because its fp32 reduction over the last axis takes a different kernel/order on a strided input. That is exactly the B3.1/B3.3 reduction-order class every batched rewrite in this engine has produced, and its binding gate is D13, which is green below.
predicted_delta: +4.0 to +7.0% timeboxed decode_heavy tok/s: 463-476 vs the accepted exp-0024 row 445.0 (merge bar 446.3). Cycle model from that row's own block (613 s, 2131 requests, 272,768 tokens): every request must be prefilled and exp-0017 admits cohorts of 6, so the box contains at least 2131/6 = ~355 grouped prefill traversals, each of which pays 264 sconv calls. At the measured in-situ saving for a 6-row group (125 ms) that is ~44 s of the 613 s box = 7.2%, i.e. ~477 tok/s; I quote a range that starts well below it because the saving per traversal scales with the group's row count and token count, and the canonical draw (randint(512,1024) words) is not exactly the 690-800 the arm used. FLOOR CASE: this is a directly measured wall-clock difference on the real engine through the real Scheduler, not an extrapolation from a microbenchmark, and it does not depend on the box forming FULL cohorts — a 1-row traversal still makes all 264 calls, just on fewer rows, so admission fragmentation (the exp-0014 failure mode) reduces the win proportionally rather than erasing it. It cannot read negative: the kernel moves strictly fewer bytes at every site shape measured, is bitwise equal to what it replaces, and the layout it hands downstream is measurably cheaper for both consumers it reaches first. The way it reads NULL is if the prefill term is a much smaller share of the canonical box than 355 traversals x 0.65 s implies — which would itself be worth knowing, and would show up as a decode-dominated box in the next iteration's ranking.

local_pregate.determinism: arm b of t_fused_sconv (two identical kernel calls bitwise equal) and arm c of t_fused_sconv_insitu (two identical fused SCHEDULES produce bitwise-identical token streams; the eager arm does too). The kernel has a fixed grid, no atomics, no autotune and no shape-dependent branching beyond the static tap count, so the kernel sequence is a pure function of the schedule. Nothing inside the CUDA-graph-captured decode step changes — the fused branch is on the prefill path only.
local_pregate.algebra: arm a is the algebra: same taps, same ascending order, same fp32 accumulate, same own-input residual, same single bf16 round — bitwise equal over 300M+ elements at every site shape and both dtypes, including a channel-major input. The only observable change is WHERE the result is stored (contiguous instead of channel-major), and arm f measures what that does: GEMMs bitwise, torch rmsnorm not.

local_pregate.memory: strictly lower: the eager chain allocated three fp32 [B,T,C] temporaries per call (the upcast, the conv1d output and the residual sum) and the kernel allocates one bf16 output. At the canonical cohort shape that is ~1.3 GB of transient allocation deleted per sconv site.
